lesson.title: Shifting Power After 1900
lesson.summary: How the Qing, Ottoman, and Russian empires collapsed and how revolutions in China, Russia, and Mexico challenged the old order.
learningGoals: Explain how internal and external factors contributed to change in various states after 1900.
Explain the causes of the collapse of empires and the revolutions in Russia, China, and Mexico.
lesson.bigIdea: Long-established empires and regimes collapsed after 1900 under the pressure of war, foreign intervention, and revolutionary movements.
lesson.context: By 1900, the Qing, Ottoman, and Russian empires had suffered defeats and faced demands for reform from within.

sections.title: The collapse of empires

blocks.text: The Qing dynasty, weakened by foreign defeats and the Boxer Rebellion, fell in a revolution in 1911; the last emperor abdicated in 1912. Sun Yat-sen led the new Republic of China, but warlords controlled much of the country.
The Ottoman Empire, defeated in World War I, ended in 1922, and Mustafa Kemal founded the Republic of Turkey in 1923.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: The end of an empire did not produce a stable state at once. China and Turkey faced years of conflict and reform.

sections.takeaway: Defeat and internal pressure brought down empires that had lasted for centuries.

sections.title: Revolutions in Russia and Mexico

blocks.text: In Russia, war losses and food shortages led the tsar to abdicate in March 1917. In November, the Bolsheviks under Lenin seized power, promising peace, land, and bread. After a civil war, they founded the Soviet Union in 1922.

The Mexican Revolution began in 1910 against the dictator Porfirio Díaz. Leaders such as Emiliano Zapata demanded land for peasants, and the Constitution of 1917 promised land reform and national control of resources.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Inequality, war, and hunger discredited old rulers, which allowed revolutionary movements promising land and bread to win support.

sections.takeaway: Revolutions in Russia and Mexico promised land and social change to peasants and workers.

connections.body: Unit 6 described the Self-Strengthening Movement and the Opium Wars. When reforms failed to protect China, revolutionaries turned against the Qing.
